title: Resource authorization slate and temporal bindings
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and spec a deployable RBAC v2 role model that supports: hierarchical resource scopes, temporal role bindings (time-limited grants), explicit deny precedence, explainable permission resolution, and first-class audit events for role changes and policy evaluations. This ticket produces the canonical schema, evaluator algorithm, SAML/SSO mapping strategy, and a migration plan from v1 role model to v2 with minimal customer disruption.
acceptance_criteria: Schema: DB tables and indexes defined for roles, role_bindings, scope_tree, permission_matrix, and audit_events; migration SQL drafted
Evaluator: deterministic algorithm implemented that computes effective permissions for a principal on a resource in under 10ms p99 for common path lengths (<=5 scope layers)
Temporal bindings: role_bindings support start_at and end_at and enforcement respects server timezone/UTC semantics
Explicit deny: deny rules take precedence in evaluator and are represented in the permission_matrix and tests
SAML mapping: group-to-role mapping extension documented with fallback behavior and example SAML assertions
Audit trail: every role/permission change emits an immutable audit_event with before/after, actor, and idempotency token; policy evaluations log explainable paths when debug flag enabled
Migration: automated migration script for customers on v1 that preserves existing effective permissions and emits migration report
technical_design:
Overview:
We adopt a capability-anchored RBAC v2 where a role is a named capability bundle (read,write,admin,manage-keys,deploy) and scope is a location in the resource hierarchy (org,project,environment). Roles are bound to principals via role_bindings that include scope_id, start_at, end_at, and binding_type (direct,delegated,service).

Schema (high level):
- roles(role_id, name, description, permissions_mask, created_by, created_at)
- scope_tree(scope_id, parent_scope_id, kind, metadata_path) -- materialized path for fast ancestry queries
- role_bindings(binding_id, role_id, principal_id, principal_type, scope_id, start_at, end_at, created_by, created_at, active_flag)
- permission_matrix(permission_id, action, resource_kind, implied_permissions_json) -- reference table used to normalize masks
- audit_events(event_id, event_type, actor_id, target_id, payload_json, created_at, seq) -- append-only; compressed JSONB payload
- effective_cache(principal_id, scope_id, effective_permissions_mask, ttl, computed_at) -- cache invalidated by binding changes

Evaluator algorithm (summary):
1) Resolve principal direct bindings at scope and ancestors by querying materialized path; short-circuit on explicit deny
2) Expand role->permissions via permission_matrix and implied permissions; apply deny-mask bitwise before allow-mask
3) Merge temporal constraints (start/end) and binding_type priorities (breakglass > admin > delegated)
4) Store explainable path when debug requested: minimal set of (binding_id, role_id, scope_distance, reason)
Complexity: O(depth + number_of_bindings_at_scope). With materialized path + proper indexes, depth usually <=5; expect stable p99 under target.

SAML/SSO mapping:
- Accept group claims and map group->role with an ordered mapping table. Mapping includes scope template (e.g., org:${SAML_org}) and fallback to global defaults.
- Support SCIM-based group sync for large orgs; when SCIM not available, fall back to signed SAML attributes.
- Edge cases: conflict resolution uses mapping priority and emits audit warning if a single principal maps to both allow and deny roles.

Audit & observability:
- All writes to roles/role_bindings emit audit_events with before/after payloads and actor metadata.
- Policy evaluation logs a short explainable path if evaluation_latency > threshold OR when request includes ?explain=true header.
- Audit_events are retained per org retention policy; we store compacted events for long-term and full events for 90 days.
decisions: Capability-based roles chosen over verbatim permission lists to simplify migration and enable implied permissions
Explicit deny masks implemented; deny always wins during merge
Materialized path used for scope_tree to optimize ancestor queries rather than recursive joins
Store audit payloads as compressed JSONB and surface via Console and audit API rather than printing to logs
Temporal bindings use server-side UTC semantics; UI will display in org locale
